key_insight: Adaptive hyperreduction accelerates finite element discovery of neural constitutive laws while preserving accuracy as network weights change.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can identify material behavior from structural reaction-force data without requiring measured full-field displacements, while accommodating arbitrary geometries and boundary conditions.
method: Combine proper orthogonal decomposition with energy-conserving sampling and weighting.
Adapt the reduced trial space and sampled elements during training using reduced-model adjoint sensitivities.
Use a neural energy architecture that guarantees polyconvexity, coercivity, and non-negativity by construction.
evidence_signal: Across two experimental datasets and one synthetic 3D example, the method reproduced reaction forces and predicted displacement fields; two-phase training fell from nine hours to 41 minutes without reported accuracy loss.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on adapting the reduced basis and element sampling as the constitutive model evolves during optimization.
paper_title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
